# dqt

> A Data Questioning Tool that tells you the what and surfaces the why. Unifies your scattered data into one source of truth. Upgrades your existing models, dashboards, and queries into a causal semantic layer you didn't have to write. Picks up on trends and surfaces business insights, all wrapped in a quality harness that puts guardrails on the AI so the reports it generates stay on-spec.

dqt is a pip-installable Python library (`pip install dqtlib`) that runs standalone in notebooks, CI pipelines, and orchestration tasks. No server required. The optional FastAPI service and Next.js dashboard add multi-tenancy and scheduling.

## Core concepts

- **Check**: binds a detector to a target column or table with optional scope, filters, and baseline config
- **Detector**: a statistical method that implements `fit(reference) → state` and `score(current, state) → DetectorResult`
- **Runner**: orchestrates fit and score operations against a warehouse adapter
- **RunResult**: returned by `runner.run()` — carries verdict, score, plain_english, details, diagnostic_sql
- **Incident**: created automatically when a run returns warn or fail — carries severity, score, opened_at, status
- **MemoryStore**: in-memory results store — no database needed for notebooks and CI
- **LocalAdapter**: wraps any pandas DataFrame — no warehouse connection needed
- **LineageGraph**: directed graph of LineageNode and LineageEdge objects — built from SQL, dbt manifests, or manually
- **SemanticManifest**: YAML-defined dataset/column descriptions loaded with `load_semantic_manifest()`
- **write_vault()**: generates an Obsidian-compatible LLM Wiki vault (raw/ + wiki/) from the semantic manifest and lineage graph

- [Lineage API](https://github.com/antonbarr-data/dqt/blob/main/docs/api/lineage.md): LineageGraph construction from SQL (sqlglot), dbt manifest ingestion, OpenLineage events, graph queries

- [Semantic layer & LLM Wiki](https://github.com/antonbarr-data/dqt/blob/main/docs/semantic-layer.md): Build your data knowledge graph from Trello tickets, SQL, and BI reports using Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern + Claude Code

## Quick usage

```python
import pandas as pd
from dqt import Check, Runner, MemoryStore
from dqt.adapters.local import LocalAdapter

df = pd.read_csv("orders.csv")
adapter = LocalAdapter({"public.orders": df})
runner = Runner(MemoryStore())

result = runner.run(Check(
    schema_name="public",
    table_name="orders",
    column_name="amount_usd",
    detector_slug="mad_outlier_fraction",
    params={"threshold": 3.5},
), adapter)

print(result.verdict)        # Verdict.pass_
print(result.score)          # 0.0082
print(result.plain_english)  # "0.82% of values are outliers — within the 1% warn threshold"
print(result.diagnostic_sql) # "amount_usd > 487.3 OR amount_usd < -12.4"
print(result.details)        # {"outlier_count": 82, "total_count": 10000, "mad": 45.2, ...}
```

## RunResult fields

verdict (Verdict: pass_/warn/fail), score (float), plain_english (str), details (dict — detector breakdown), diagnostic_sql (str|None — WHERE clause for failing rows), check_id (UUID), detector_slug (str), run_id (UUID), started_at (datetime), finished_at (datetime)

## Incident fields

id (UUID), check_id (UUID), run_id (UUID), severity (Verdict: warn/fail), score (float), plain_english (str), opened_at (datetime), resolved_at (datetime|None), status ("open"|"resolved")

## Querying MemoryStore after runs

```python
runs = store.list_runs(check.id, limit=50)
incidents = store.list_incidents()                       # all incidents
open_incidents = store.list_incidents(status="open")     # open only
check_incidents = store.list_incidents(check_id=check.id)
triggering_run = store.get_run(incident.run_id)
```

## Causal discovery results

```python
from dqt.causality import CausalRunner, CausalConfig

dag = CausalRunner(config=CausalConfig(method="pcmci_plus", max_lag=4)).discover(metric_panel)

for edge in dag.edges:
    print(edge.source, "→", edge.target)
    print(edge.lag_weeks, edge.confidence, edge.e_value)  # e_value < 1.5 = fragile

attribution = dag.shapley_attribution(target="weekly_transaction_volume", t="2024-04-15", metric_panel=metric_panel)
parents = dag.parents("weekly_transaction_volume")
```

## CausalEdge fields

source (str), target (str), kind ("causality"|"aggregates"|"filters"|"joins"|"derives"), lag_weeks (int|None), confidence (float 0–1), e_value (float|None — sensitivity to unobserved confounders), description (str|None), method_stats (dict — Granger F, Transfer Entropy, etc.)

## AI explanation output

```python
from dqt.agent import AgentExplainer

explanation = AgentExplainer().explain(incident=incident, adapter=adapter, dag=dag)

print(explanation.plain_english)   # full narrative
print(explanation.confidence)      # 0.87
print(explanation.level)           # "intervention" (Pearl ladder: association/intervention/counterfactual)

for ev in explanation.evidence:
    print(ev.kind, ev.label, ev.detail, ev.source_ref)

for q in explanation.follow_up_questions:
    print(q)
```

## Explanation fields

plain_english (str), confidence (float), level ("association"|"intervention"|"counterfactual"), evidence (list[Evidence] — kind/label/detail/source_ref), follow_up_questions (list[str]), incident_id (UUID), model (str), token_usage (dict)

## All detector slugs

mad_outlier_fraction, double_mad_outlier_fraction, zscore_outlier_fraction, adjusted_boxplot_fraction, auto_outlier_fraction, isolation_forest_fraction, ks_pvalue, stl_residual_zscore, null_fraction, completeness, uniqueness, volume, numeric_mean, value_in_range, set_membership, set_exclusion, regex_match, string_length_range, string_case_violation, date_format, freshness_seconds_behind, monotonicity, sql_assertion_violation, column_pair_comparison, composite_uniqueness, row_count_in_range, max_in_range, min_in_range, median_in_range, sum_in_range, stddev_in_range, cardinality_in_range, quantile_in_range, date_part_missing_fraction, referential_integrity_rate, schema_change

## Check model fields

schema_name (str, required), table_name (str, required), column_name (str|None), detector_slug (str, required), params (dict, default {}), sample_n (int, default 100_000), sampling_pct (float|None), scope (CheckScope|None), filters (list[CheckFilter]), baseline (BaselineConfig|None)

## CheckScope fields

mode: "entire" | "incremental" | "custom" — key_col (str, for incremental) — since (ISO date or "last_run") — custom_sql (WHERE clause)

## Lineage: building a LineageGraph

```python
from dqt.lineage import LineageGraph, LineageNode, LineageEdge

graph = LineageGraph(nodes=[
    LineageNode(id="gigler_transactions", kind="dataset", label="Transactions"),
    LineageNode(id="weekly_transaction_volume", kind="metric", label="Weekly Volume",
                meta={"description": "Sum of completed transactions per week", "unit": "count"}),
], edges=[
    LineageEdge(source="gigler_transactions.amount_usd", target="weekly_transaction_volume", kind="aggregates"),
    LineageEdge(source="marketing_campaigns.spend_usd", target="weekly_transaction_volume",
                kind="causality", confidence=0.72, lag_weeks=2,
                description="Acquisition spend drives volume with 2-week lag"),
])
```

## Lineage: parsing from SQL (sqlglot)

```python
from dqt.lineage import parse_sql_lineage, merge_graphs
import pathlib

# Single SQL string
graph = parse_sql_lineage(sql, dialect="bigquery")

# Multiple files
graphs = [parse_sql_lineage(p.read_text(), dialect="clickhouse")
          for p in pathlib.Path("raw/sql/").glob("*.sql")]
graph = merge_graphs(graphs)
```

Supported dialects: duckdb, postgres, bigquery, clickhouse, snowflake, spark, mysql, trino

## Lineage: dbt manifest ingestion

```python
from dqt.lineage import load_dbt_manifest

graph = load_dbt_manifest("target/manifest.json")
# Extracts: model/source nodes, column-level depends_on edges, semantic_models.yml metrics
```

## Lineage: OpenLineage ingestion

```python
from dqt.lineage import load_openlineage_events

graph = load_openlineage_events("openlineage_events.ndjson")
graph = load_openlineage_events(marquez_url="http://localhost:5000", namespace="my_pipeline")
```

## Lineage: graph queries

```python
upstreams   = graph.upstreams("weekly_transaction_volume")
downstreams = graph.downstreams("gigler_transactions.amount_usd")  # blast radius
path        = graph.path("marketing_campaigns.spend_usd", "weekly_transaction_volume")
causal      = [e for e in graph.edges if e.kind == "causality"]
```

## Vault: LLM Wiki structure

The vault is an Obsidian-compatible Markdown knowledge graph. `raw/` = source-of-truth documents you own. `wiki/` = synthesised knowledge generated by dqt or Claude Code.

```
vault/
├── raw/
│   ├── datasets/<id>.md          # dataset metadata + known issues
│   └── columns/<dataset>/<col>.md  # per-column atomic note
└── wiki/
    ├── metrics/<id>.md           # metric definition + lineage (generated)
    ├── lineage/causality.md      # discovered causal edges (generated)
    └── datasets/<id>.md          # synthesised dataset knowledge (generated)
```

## Vault: raw/ Markdown frontmatter

Dataset note (`raw/datasets/<id>.md`):
```yaml
---
id: gigler_transactions
kind: dataset
owner: platform-analytics@gigler.com
domain: platform
freshness_sla_hours: 4
classification: internal
tags: [transactions, platform]
---
```

Column note (`raw/columns/<dataset>/<column>.md`):
```yaml
---
dataset: gigler_transactions
column: amount_usd
kind: column
pii: false
classification: internal
unit: USD
nullable: false
tags: [financial, core]
---
```

## Vault: generating

```python
from dqt.semantic import load_semantic_manifest
from dqt.lineage import LineageGraph, LineageEdge, write_vault

manifest = load_semantic_manifest("semantic.yaml")
graph = LineageGraph(nodes=[...], edges=[...])
write_vault(manifest, graph, vault_dir="vault/", vault_title="My Knowledge Graph")
```

## Vault: extending with custom node types

```python
from dqt.lineage import LineageNode, LineageEdge

graph.nodes.append(LineageNode(
    id="gtm_001_revenue_report",
    kind="report",   # custom kind — rendered as generic wiki note
    label="GTM-001 Weekly Revenue Report",
    meta={"requestor": "Sarah Chen", "date": "2024-03-15"},
))
graph.edges.append(LineageEdge(
    source="gigler_transactions.amount_usd",
    target="gtm_001_revenue_report",
    kind="aggregates",
))
# → writes vault/wiki/reports/gtm_001_revenue_report.md with [[wiki-links]]
```

## YAML source types

csv (path + table_name), parquet (path + table_name), duckdb (database), postgres (connection_string)

## Use with Claude Code (recommended)

Three plugins turn Claude Code into a grounded data-quality engineer for dqt:

**1. Context7** (https://claude.com/plugins/context7) — connects Claude Code to dqt's live documentation and source. Claude always has the current API, all detector slugs, and the exact YAML schema — not a training-data snapshot from months ago. Ask Claude Code to write checks, pick detectors, or debug failures and it grounds every answer in the actual dqt code.

**2. Superpowers** (https://claude.com/plugins/superpowers) — gives Claude Code structured agentic workflows for planning and executing multi-step tasks. Useful for building out a full check suite, generating a semantic layer from scratch, or TDD-ing a detector config.

**3. Warehouse MCP** — each warehouse publishes its own MCP server. Example: mcp-clickhouse (https://github.com/ClickHouse/mcp-clickhouse) for ClickHouse. Connect Claude Code to your warehouse and it can inspect live schemas, sample real column distributions, and generate dqt checks and `semantic.yaml` grounded in your actual data.
